title: anthropics/claude-code — Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows - all through natural language commands.
content:
Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands. Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.
Learn more in the official documentation.
Note
Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below.
For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the setup documentation.
- 
Install Claude Code: MacOS/Linux (Recommended): curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bashHomebrew (MacOS/Linux): brew install --cask claude-code Windows (Recommended): irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex WinGet (Windows): winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode NPM (Deprecated): npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
- 
Navigate to your project directory and run claude .
This repository includes several Claude Code plugins that extend functionality with custom commands and agents. See the plugins directory for detailed documentation on available plugins.
We welcome your feedback. Use the /bug command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a GitHub issue.
Join the Claude Developers Discord to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community.
When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the /bug command.
See our data usage policies.
We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training.
For full details, please review our Commercial Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

report.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code is a terminal-native agentic coding tool that uses natural language to execute tasks, explain code, and manage git workflows.
report.background: AI coding assistants have evolved from simple autocomplete (GitHub Copilot) to chat-based helpers (ChatGPT, Claude) and now to autonomous agents. Claude Code, launched by Anthropic in early 2025, exemplifies this shift: it lives in the terminal, understands entire codebases, and performs routine tasks, git operations, and code explanations via natural language. It can be used in terminals, IDEs, or by tagging @claude on GitHub. The repo recently deprecated npm installation in favor of curl, Homebrew, and WinGet, signaling maturing distribution. It also bundles plugins for custom commands and agents, and includes privacy safeguards like limited data retention and no training on user feedback. This positions Anthropic against Cursor, Devin, and OpenAI's Codex in the growing agentic coding market.
key_points: Terminal-native agentic workflow: Claude Code operates from the command line, understands your codebase, and executes routine tasks, explains complex code, and handles git workflows using natural language. It also works in IDEs and integrates with GitHub via @claude mentions.

Installation overhaul: npm installation is deprecated. Recommended methods now include a curl script (macOS/Linux), Homebrew cask, PowerShell script (Windows), and WinGet. This reflects broader platform support and a move toward more robust distribution channels.

Plugin extensibility: The repository includes plugins that extend functionality with custom commands and agents. Developers can tailor Claude Code to specific workflows, automate repetitive actions, and integrate with existing toolchains.

Privacy and data usage: Anthropic collects usage data, conversation data, and feedback, but implements safeguards: limited retention for sensitive information, restricted access to session data, and a policy against using feedback for model training. Full details are in the Commercial Terms and Privacy Policy.
Community and feedback: Users can report bugs via the /bug command or GitHub issues, and join the Claude Developers Discord for help and discussion. This fosters an active ecosystem around the tool.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Claude Code reinforces the shift from assistive autocomplete to autonomous, agentic coding, raising the bar for tools like Cursor, Devin, and GitHub Copilot Workspace. It signals that terminal-native, natural-language-driven development is becoming a standard expectation. For developers, it promises faster routine tasks, git workflow automation, and code explanation, but requires trust in AI to modify code and execute commands—making privacy and auditability critical. For regular users, the indirect benefit is faster software delivery and potentially higher-quality applications. The npm deprecation also shows rapid iteration, urging developers to adapt installation practices and avoid outdated methods.
report.tools: To explore similar tools, check out Aider (open-source terminal AI pair programmer), OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin), Cline (VS Code agent), Continue, and Cursor. For Claude Code specifically, see the official documentation, the plugins directory for custom commands and agents, and join the Claude Developers Discord. GitHub Copilot Workspace and Devin are commercial alternatives worth watching.
